expected_exception: A window normally requires glazing/glass panes, but louvred, jalousie and solid-panel 'windows' admit no glass; fixed (non-operable) windows are an exception to the openable-light requirement.
A door normally requires a fire rating only on escape routes and compartment lines; ordinary internal doors are exempt, and some openings use shutters or curtains rather than a hinged leaf.
A roof normally requires falls to drainage, but inverted/ballasted and green roofs handle water differently; pitched roofs shed water without internal outlets.
A staircase normally requires guarding and uniform risers, but loft and spiral stairs, and stairs serving limited-use areas, are subject to relaxed dimensional rules.
A foundation normally requires bearing below the frost line on firm strata, but raft and piled foundations on poor ground, and rock sites, are recognised exceptions.
A load-bearing wall must not be removed without substitute support, except where a beam or transfer structure is introduced to carry the load above.
A beam normally requires support at both ends, but cantilever beams are supported at one end only; deflection limits relax for non-brittle finishes.
A wall lintel is normally required over an opening in a load-bearing wall, but non-load-bearing partition walls may not require a lintel in some configurations.
A damp-proof course normally requires mortar bedding, except pre-formed plastic DPCs and liquid-applied (bitumen-based or polymer-modified cementitious) DPCs, which are laid or coated without mortar.
A balcony edge above a drop normally requires 1100mm guarding, except for low-level thresholds and Juliet balconies where the door itself forms the barrier.
A family kitchen normally requires full cabinetry, except in hospitality settings (e.g. a hotel room kitchenette) where open shelving or minimal storage is used instead.
A family bathroom normally contains a toilet directly within the room, except in commercial/public hospitality settings where partitioned or separate toilet stalls are required instead.
A master bedroom normally requires a dedicated HVAC system, except in mild climates where natural ventilation suffices, or where a central/ductless system serves the room instead.
A corridor on an escape route normally requires fire protection and minimum width, except for short dead-end lengths within the permitted travel distance.
A drainage system normally requires falls to a sewer, except where pumped/sump systems serve below-sewer levels and soakaways serve surface water on permeable ground.
An HVAC system normally requires mechanical heating and cooling, except in passive/naturally-ventilated buildings and mild climates where one or both are omitted.
A ventilation system normally requires mechanical supply and extract, except where natural ventilation through openable windows meets the requirement.
A fire suppression system (sprinklers) is normally required in large or high-rise buildings, except for small buildings and uses below the floor-area and height thresholds.
